unresolved: Full texts and underlying site datasets remain needed for Jones, Raab, Benson, Gardner, Briere and other abstract/metadata-only entries before adding finer site histories.
Foster/Choice bibliographic identity requires verification; no southeastern abandonment, buffer-zone or river relocation claims accepted from this item or the Barnes review.
Galloway and Pei are broad comparative works; verify study population and geographic coverage before applying them to specific Indigenous North American communities.
No exact archaeological coordinates or population totals were verified for new regional records; both remain absent.
No individual Northeast migrant origins, destinations or refuge population estimates were established in the source scope accessed.
corrections: The headline that medieval megadroughts drove continent-wide depopulation turns correlation and regional hypotheses into a universal causal fact. Climate effects are spatially variable and mediated by institutions, subsistence and social relations.
Stager documents severe Northeast droughts around 1260–1330 and 1360–1390. The synthesis’s settled hydroclimatic-refuge and migrant-absorption narrative is not accepted.
Friesen explicitly finds no warming link for Thule expansion around 1250; social drivers are preferred. Late Dorset expansion and later Inuit southern redistribution are separate episodes.
Bird’s abandonment interval extends to 1450 and is staggered. It must not be compressed into a universal 1200s collapse or used to override Cahokia site chronology.
Benson drought intervals are discrete; no continuous drought from 990 to 1297, complete Fremont/Ancestral Pueblo abandonment everywhere, or automatic high mortality is established.
McCool uses settlement defensibility as a conflict proxy and models interacting social/climatic variables; it is not direct proof of warfare at every settlement.

Gardner is a 2005 UNLV dissertation, not a 2019 journal paper. Kelly is print 2013 with 2012 online publication; McCool is volume 91 (2026) with 2025 online publication; Briere prairie-forest is volume 41 (2023), despite 2022 supplied metadata.
Barnes is a book review, not Cable’s primary monograph. Foster’s Choice DOI is unresolved and not accepted as a primary site source.
Doering is already represented by alaska-doering-climate-counterpoint; the repeat citation is not a new independent finding or evidence for a Thule warming narrative.
